title: Mekhela sador weaving
summary: The mekhela sador is the two-piece garment of Assam: a wrap-around skirt, the mekhela, and a long draped cloth, the sador. Both are handwoven, mostly by women, in silks such as muga, a natural golden-yellow silk that is made only in Assam. Flowers, leaves and other motifs from nature are woven into the cloth with an extra weft thread.
howToPlay: Pick a thread colour and a pattern shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the cloth to weave that shape there; it is mirrored on the other side of the centre line.
Copy the motif pattern shown on the card, then press Check.
rules: The pattern is mirrored left and right, so every shape you place also appears on its partner square.
A square counts only when its shape and its thread colour both match the pattern you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Muga silk comes from silkworms that feed on local trees in the Brahmaputra valley, and its colour deepens and glows with age. Weaving is part of many households in Assam, where a loom stands on the veranda of the house.
